notes: Overall a strong, well-structured implementation. Architectural adherence is good: EventBus is used for task.assigned, task.statusChanged, and comment.added; services own their own Maps; the router is the sole HTTP handler. However, there are two notable architectural tensions: (1) The router performs direct cross-service calls for validation (e.g., userService.getUser() before taskService.assignTask(), projectService.getProject() before taskService.createTask()), which technically violates rule 1 ('no direct service-to-service calls') even if it is the router doing it rather than a service — the spirit of the rule is that inter-service data flow goes through the bus, but here the router acts as an orchestrator/mediator which is a common and defensible pattern; (2) cascade deletes (deleteTasksByProject, deleteCommentsByTask) are orchestrated directly by the router calling multiple services, bypassing the event bus — a project.deleted event could have driven this instead, which would be cleaner. On constraint compliance: rule 5 (no external npm deps) is respected; rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly enforced with same-status treated as a no-op rather than an error (debatable but documented); rule 6 (each service in its own file) is satisfied. The status same-status no-op is a minor design choice that could be argued either way. Completeness is high: all CRUD operations are present for all entities, all three event types are published and consumed, notifications support listing/filtering/mark-as-read, and a thorough demo script exercises all paths including error cases and cascade deletes. Code quality is excellent: consistent TypeScript interfaces in types.ts, clean error propagation, good use of generics in EventBus, idiomatic Map usage, immutable-style service constructors, proper Content-Length headers, snapshot iteration in event bus for safe mid-iteration unsubscribe, and clear comments throughout. Minor issues: the router catches all non-'not found' service errors as 400 which could mask genuine 500s; the demo's 'todo→todo same-status' test case comment is slightly misleading; deleteCommentsByTask is not called when a task is deleted via the project cascade path (only deleteTasksByProject is called, skipping comment cleanup for cascaded tasks).
